# toSemanticDocument

> Convert Markdown to a semantic document.

<section class="intro">

A semantic document is a versioned, JSON-serializable intermediate representation which preserves Markdown structure while making document semantics explicit. The representation is intended for downstream consumers such as notebook renderers, search indexers, and interactive documentation tooling.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var toSemanticDocument = require( '@stdlib/_tools/semantic-document/from-markdown' );
```

#### toSemanticDocument( markdown\[, options] )

Converts a Markdown string or [`Buffer`][@stdlib/buffer/ctor] to a semantic document.

```javascript
var markdown = '# abs\n\n> Compute an absolute value.';

var out = toSemanticDocument( markdown );
```

The function supports the following options:

-   **mode**: conversion mode. Must be one of the following:

    -   `'permissive'`: preserve unknown content and return diagnostics.
    -   `'strict'`: perform the same conversion as `'permissive'` and raise an exception when the result contains an error diagnostic. The error exposes the partial document via an `error.document` property.

    Default: `'permissive'`.

-   **profile**: semantic profile. Must be one of the following:

    -   `'generic'`: preserve standalone raw HTML without interpreting stdlib section wrappers, maintenance comments, or execution directives.
    -   `'readme'`: interpret stdlib section wrappers, maintenance comments, or execution directives.
    -   `'tutorial'`: interpret stdlib section wrappers, maintenance comments, or execution directives, group root headings below the title into nested tutorial topics, classify JavaScript code as candidate executable examples.

    Default: `'readme'`.

-   **includePositions**: boolean indicating whether to include source ranges. Default: `true`.

-   **includeSourceSlices**: boolean indicating whether to include exact source slices. Default: `false`.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   Reference-style links and images are resolved in projected MDAST fragments. Ordered definitions remain available under `document.resources.definitions`.
-   Unknown raw HTML is preserved as a `raw` semantic node. Characterized maintenance markup is recorded in the source-accounting ledger.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```javascript
var toSemanticDocument = require( '@stdlib/_tools/semantic-document/from-markdown' );

var markdown = [
    '# abs',
    '',
    '> Compute an absolute value.',
    '',
    '<section class="usage">',
    '',
    '## Usage',
    '',
    '```javascript',
    'var abs = require( \'@stdlib/math/base/special/abs\' );',
    '```',
    '',
    '</section>',
    '',
    '<!-- /.usage -->'
].join( '\n' );

var out = toSemanticDocument( markdown );

console.log( out.titleRef );
// => 'heading[0]'

console.log( out.children[ 2 ].role );
// => 'usage'

console.log( out.children[ 2 ].children[ 1 ].role );
// => 'setup'
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
